correctness.rationale: An exact formal-series identity (1-x)^p ≡1-x^p-p Σ_{j=1}^{p-1}x^j/j mod p^2 proves the result by geometric-series division. The second correction term cannot contribute to degree dp. The first contributes zero if p does not divide 2d+1, and otherwise -H_{(p-1)/2}; the latter equals (2^p-2)/p mod p by binomial expansion of 2^p. Boundary d=0 and p=3 included. Independent exact coefficient algorithms agreed on 319 tested (p,d) cases, 33 exceptional.

originality.rationale: A complete two-branch prime-square formula for all central odd-nomial coefficients at prime index was not located after direct and equivalent-form searches and comparison with the closest archival primary sources. Sun establishes a weaker modulo-p lemma for trinomials; Rudolph-Lilith–Muller provide analytic trace formulas but no prime-square law; Mellit–Vlasenko impose a Newton-polytope hypothesis failing for radii at least two. Search absence is not mathematical proof of priority and an older equivalent identity remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated classical identity for prime rows of uniform odd-nomial coefficients could imply the complete formula under another name.
The full 2015 journal continuation with Dirichlet kernels was not accessible; its abstract alone does not support a claim that its entire contents lack the same congruence.
Independent mathematical audit and historical-priority certification have not been performed.

value.rationale: A natural and complete two-parameter prime-square classification for central odd-nomial (equivalently symmetric-walk return) counts, with an unexpected singular exceptional branch determined solely by divisibility of alphabet size and the base-two Fermat quotient. Extends beyond the classical trinomial and pentanomial examples and provides a reusable coefficient method; not just a table recomputation. The exact branch can coincide at Wieferich primes, which is explicitly acknowledged.
